# Independent focused legal audit — House/Senate oversight blueprint

Review date: November 7, 2026 (Japan time). Reviewer: independent legal-research agent. Scope: `docs/01-hub-and-authorities.md`, `docs/02-state-referrals.md`, `docs/05-litigation-and-privilege.md`, and `templates/appendix-a-house-rules.md`. Existing files were not modified.

## Result and limits

No critical defect was found in the sampled priority propositions: the documents distinguish legislative oversight from prosecution, maintain statutory compartments for tax/SAR information, recognize Senate authority separately, and label the resolution as proposed. This is a focused AI source audit, not an exhaustive current-law search, professional legal opinion, Parliamentarian approval, or verification of every state statute. A whole-document “legally vetted” label would exceed this review.

## Findings requiring implementation

### L01 — Explain Senate authority visibly; preserve separate legal owners

Severity: material usability/authority clarification. The current substantive chapter is correct but the Senate appears only in a compact row and one technical paragraph. Add an immediately understandable route from the diagram: House committees and Senate committees can investigate matters within their own jurisdictions; each issues its own authorized process. Shared research support does not merge those powers. Senate Rule XXV addresses jurisdictions; Rule XXVI(1) supplies committee/subcommittee hearing, subpoena, testimony and investigation authority; each committee must adopt its own procedures under XXVI(2). PSI is an existing investigative subcommittee, not a proposed creation of this project. Its 119th procedures are a current baseline, while 120th delegations must be verified after organization.

Primary sources checked:
- Senate Standing Rules, XXV–XXVI: https://www.rules.senate.gov/rules-of-the-senate
- Senate overview: https://www.senate.gov/about/powers-procedures/investigations.htm
- PSI jurisdiction and link to 119th rules: https://www.hsgac.senate.gov/subcommittees/investigations/
- 119th HSGAC rules and Senate Resolution 94, committee print S. Prt. 119-11: https://www.hsgac.senate.gov/wp-content/uploads/Rules-of-Procedure-HSGAC-119.pdf

### L02 — Keep enforcement approvals out of a generic wheel connector

Severity: material design constraint; existing text passes. 28 U.S.C. §1365 supplies a Senate-specific civil mechanism and contains a qualified executive-official exception. 2 U.S.C. §288b(b) requires a Senate resolution to direct Senate Legal Counsel to bring a subpoena-enforcement action under §288d. A House rule or project ticket cannot grant that authority. The existing text correctly preserves this distinction. Do not simplify the landing page to “the hub subpoenas everyone” or “the hub directly prosecutes.”

Primary sources checked:
- https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?edition=prelim&num=0&req=granuleid%3AUSC-prelim-title28-section1365
- https://uscode.house.gov/us/usc/119-118/t2/s288b/

### L03 — Complete the BSA request-purpose description

Severity: small textual correction. In `docs/01-hub-and-authorities.md`, §5, replace the summary that a §1010.950(c) request states “the particular information, purpose, and official need” with: “the particular information desired, the criminal, tax or regulatory purpose, and the official need.” The regulation is discretionary; do not imply a mandatory bulk-release entitlement. BOI remains separately governed. The chapter already correctly requires accommodation and separates underlying bank records from protected reports.

Primary sources checked:
- Official CFR §1010.950(c), annual 2024 baseline, with live recheck required: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2024-title31-vol3/pdf/CFR-2024-title31-vol3-part1010.pdf
- Treasury Order 180-02, January 17, 2025, particularly §3(c)–(e): https://home.treasury.gov/about/general-information/orders-and-directives/treasury-order-180-02

### L04 — Tax compartment language is sound; expose the limit in plain language

Severity: material presentation requirement; existing text passes. Section 6103(f)(1) gives the named tax-committee chairs a written-request route, with the identifiable-taxpayer closed-session condition. Other committees use the specially authorized route in (f)(3), and (f)(4) treats their examiners and onward submission differently. There is no generic “all spokes share all tax data” permission. Suggested short explanation: “Tax returns and SARs stay in separately authorized compartments. A shared catalog is not unrestricted access.” Keep the statutory detail available on expansion.

Primary source checked: https://uscode.house.gov/us/usc/119-118/t26/s6103/ (§6103(a), (f)(1)–(4)).

### L05 — A landing poll must not prejudge crimes or purport to authorize process

Severity: material editorial/legal-risk correction to the proposed new feature. Prefer a dismissible invitation to explore documented oversight questions over a forced accusatory poll. If a question is retained, use “Should Congress examine credible evidence of misconduct and failures of federal law?” Link “oversight topics” to source-based research questions; do not label every listed topic an administration crime. A poll response is neither evidence nor institutional authorization. Separate allegations, official findings, pending cases, enacted law, and proposed inquiries. Names in records or contact lists do not establish culpability. Survivor/minor privacy requires specific review for any Epstein-related material.

Primary sources checked for purpose and rights: *Watkins v. United States*, 354 U.S. 178, 187–215 (1957), https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USREPORTS-354/pdf/USREPORTS-354-178.pdf ; *Trump v. Mazars USA, LLP*, 591 U.S. 848, 862–871 (2020), https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/19pdf/19-715_febh.pdf .

### L06 — Show the actual scope of machine review

Severity: release-process requirement. Recommended statuses: draft created; primary-source check completed for listed claims; independent reviewer findings resolved; qualified human legal review pending/completed with named scope. A signature, source URL resolving, or three model votes does not establish legal accuracy. Preserve objections, missing sources, and contrary evidence. Do not promote a document to “vetted” merely because an agent checked it. The existing state-referral chapter already separates allegation, inference, evidence, independent prosecutorial decisions, taint and restrictions; retain those distinctions in cards and tickets.

## Release boundary

The model House resolution requires Parliamentarian/Legislative Counsel conforming review against the actual organizational package. No private publisher can adopt it, appoint committee personnel, issue process, guarantee judicial expedition, or authorize a prosecutor. State-law elements and territorial nexus remain matter-specific. Keep the public research network separate from protected congressional evidence and confidential whistleblower intake.
